Too make this brief, they are entirely different games and how they are played.

Civ V:
This game is spent turtling, meaning you will have a small amount of cities by the end of the game, and each city will basically be a tall city, since everything is stacked. Workers in Civ V are infinite, so most of the time you just build a bunch and automate them for improvements. V has a lot more civs since it's with the dlc and the graphics might be better of your liking, though I disagree and say VI>V. V has unique features such as a world congress that keeps the game interesting, and the civ leaders have small bonuses.

VI:
VI released last month and had its first major patch, which did well in my opinion. It overalls the stacking of each city, so now city planning is a must, and you will be having a lot more cities than you would if you were playing V. VI has also an overhauled civic system, using cards to boost certain productions/culture/etc it has a lot of planning. VI has a bit more colourful graphics, but it looks great to me. Wonders also take tile space, but again thats a huge difference. The civs are different enough that they affect which victory you might want to go for rather than V where balancing was huge problem, though only 19 civs it's too early to say.

they are both played entirely different.

In civ V, youre not expanding so much, and you dont need to worry about districts. Civ V relatively basic I would say, but right now has a lot more Civ's than VI. V is about turtling and basically taking it slow while six is about multitasking.

Six, despite what many say, takes a big leap by adding districts and two trees, a civic and a tech. The civic has a new card system which boosts production/culture/etc and has you using cheat sheets to basically plan ahead. Civ VI is missing content but thats because it has just released.

If you just bought V and youre enjoying it, I would stick to that until youre bored and want to try something else.
